title: Playing the country club where he had caddied for Miss Krueger
summary: The heiress recognises the dressed-up drummer, pesters him all night, and Greer finally admits he was her caddy and refuses her offer of his old job.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: So now -- I forgot all about her, we're playing this Deer Country Club, all the white boys and me and we had a thing we did -- well, we had one white girl, sang. We used to sing by theirself. I'd sing by myself, and then a couple of them would sing and we had a trio -- two white boys, a white boy, the girl and me. Got up to sing. So now the people coming in to the dance and right on the ringside is this broad, this Miss Krueger. Big party.
Remember now, she never seen me dressed up. So now she come in and we played the first set and I noticed --

you know when someone is staring at you. She stared at me, because I'm the only colored there, with all these white cats. So she looked at me, now, she ain't drunk yet. But something in her mind said, I know him. So she asked the waiter, What's the drummer's name?" The waiter said, "I don't know, miss." This is the first time they played here."

That don't satisfy her. She asked the maître'd, "What's that drummer's name?" He said, "I don't know, miss, I never seen him. This is the first time the boy has played. Are you enjoying it." "Very much", because we could play, see, we could play and sing too. So now she ain't satisfied. She comes up to me and says, "I beg your pardon, but don't I know you?" I say, "I'm very sorry, Miss, but you don't know me. This is the first I've ever been here. You don't know me." "I could swear you look just like a boy that caddied for me." I say, "couldn't be me. I ain't got no brother, he don't caddy for nobody."

Now, she's drinking and she ain't satisfied. If she came up to me once, she came up to me about six times. Now she's real drunk and said, "I know you, so what did I tell her. No, I didn't tell her I didn't have no brother, so the last time she come up, I said, "Oh, you must be the lady my young brother caddied for." I laid that fast one on her. She look at me, she ate it up. She ate that up. Now, she's so drunk and she's so bewildered, I began to feel sorry for her. So the

last time I seen her she cursed me out, told me I was fired so I went -- she (unintelligible) sitting there drinking so I went over to her, I said "I am tired of masquerading", I said, "I used to caddy for you."
I went over to her table. She said, I knew it. She thought I was -------. She told all her friends, all over the place with all her friends, "You see that drummer? he was my caddy."

Chest is way out. so the last thing she say, you got your job back, you be on the first tee tomorrow with my bags. I said, "Lady, I'm very sorry, but I'm a professional, I don't caddy no more. I'm a professional, I don't caddy for nobody."
